notable_absence.finding: cbdatarecovery.md never links to, or names, any cbbackupmgr page, backup:archive, or backup:repository, even though its own OPERATIONS DURING MAJOR CLUSTER CONFIGURATION CHANGES section reuses cbbackupmgr's exact wording ('performing a backup or performing a restore whilst changing the TLS configuration/security settings is unsupported') and its examples' error-handling shares cbbackupmgr's own remap vocabulary almost verbatim (--map-data, the `_default` scope restriction). Despite the strong family resemblance in wording, the page frames cbdatarecovery purely as reading a raw Couchbase Server data directory ('The path to a Couchbase Server data directory') - never as consuming a cbbackupmgr backup archive at all. The two tools appear to be siblings by implementation (shared flag vocabulary, shared constraint text) but the documentation draws no explicit line between them.

cross_component_finding: This page is the clearest evidence in the round-20 tools batch for the 'same-round self-fork' risk the batch instructions warned about, resolved by REUSE rather than re-minting: its OPERATIONS DURING MAJOR CLUSTER CONFIGURATION CHANGES section and its CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION (MTLS AUTHENTICATION) section are both near-verbatim restatements of mechanisms already extracted elsewhere in the corpus (backup:major-cluster-configuration-change from cbbackupmgr.json; auth-mechanism:x509-certificate from cbbackupmgr-generate.json and the security/authentication pages). Both were reused here, and the same two ids recur identically on cbexport.md/cbimport.md (the configuration-change constraint) and cbexport-json.md/cbimport-csv.md/cbimport-json.md (the mTLS section) later in this same batch - checked against candidate-evidence.py each time rather than re-minted per page.
cross_product_finding: No Capella page in the corpus mentions cbdatarecovery or an equivalent raw-data-directory recovery path; cloud/reference/command-line-tools.json's tool:cbdatarecovery entry is a bare seeAlso pointer straight back to this Server page with no Capella-specific behaviour described. Consistent with the batch framing: this is a pure Server-only disaster-recovery tool with no Capella twin, UI or otherwise.
